gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the maker's solar panel stops charging the battery below 32°F (0°C). Kiwibit says its panel "will not charge the battery below 0°C", and Birdfy puts the solar-charging range at 32–104°F. Both feeders still run below freezing, Birdfy to 14°F and Kiwibit to −4°F, so through a freezing spell the battery only drains and is not refilled, however sunny it is.
standout_why: I opened birdfeederlab.com, feederfield.com and reviewed.com. BirdFeederLab only says the panel 'may not fully keep up' on short, overcast winter days and needs 4–6 hours of direct sun. Feeder Field says 'lithium batteries hold less charge in the cold' and plans for winter USB-C top-ups, and it notes that its 14°F and −5°F figures are operating ranges, not charging limits. Reviewed.com says nothing about winter or cold charging. None of them says that charging stops below freezing. The two cited pages, WIRED and Good Housekeeping, would not load for me, by WebFetch or by curl, so I could not check them.
decides: This settles whether 'solar powered' works year-round. In a yard that stays below 32°F for days, a solar feeder from any of these makers runs on its battery alone. It still works, but you have to charge it indoors by hand. So in cold climates battery size matters more than panel wattage. My own reasoning, which no source states: Birdfy's 9,000 mAh feeders (Feeder 2 series, Feeder Metal 2 4K) should outlast the 5,000 mAh Soliom BF08 and Bird Buddy's 3,800–3,900 mAh units on a cold, non-charging stretch. In mild climates the finding changes nothing.

The page names no model, and it says 'all Birdfy products are compatible with solar panels.'

findings.label: Cold-weather battery behavior
findings.value: Battery drains faster below 32°F (0°C); cameras operate to −4°F (−20°C); warm the module to room temperature before charging
findings.note: Quotes: 'any extended exposure to temperatures below 32°F / 0°C will cause the battery to drain faster', 'Always warm the module to room temperature before charging', 'Charge the camera indoors at room temperature', and 'Prolonged exposure below –4°F (–20°C) can even lead to permanent battery degradation.' Bird Buddy does not state a solar-roof cutoff temperature.

findings.label: Store-inside threshold
findings.value: Below −5°F / −20°C or above 120°F / 50°C, temporarily store the feeder inside
findings.note: This is an operating and storage limit, not a charging limit. The page gives no charging temperature.
